top_stories.title: Coldcard firmware flaw drains ~1,082 BTC (~$70M) from Bitcoin self-custody users
points: A seed-generation vulnerability (seed = the master secret from which a wallet's private keys, the credentials that authorize Bitcoin transfers, are derived) let attackers reconstruct keys and empty wallets.
TLDR Crypto reports 1,082 BTC (~$70.2M) taken from nearly 1,200 addresses; CMC Spotlight puts confirmed losses at over $50M.
Affected devices span Coldcard Mk3/Mk4/Mk5 firmware versions — Coldcard is a popular hardware wallet, a dedicated offline device meant to keep keys away from internet-connected computers.
Maker Coinkite shipped emergency patched firmware and urges all users to update, generate fresh seeds, and test with a small transaction before moving full balances.
Incident revives the tension between keeping wallets 'air-gapped' (physically isolated from networks) and safely delivering firmware updates.

unique_angles.point: Coinkite's CEO suggested the bug may have been found via AI-assisted code review, implying a new attack surface for hardware wallet makers.
Links to a Galaxy Research technical analysis of the vulnerability.
Says exploitation generally required physical or USB access, though some reports hint at remote vectors.
Notes Coldcard also patched vulnerabilities in 2023 and 2024, and that rival hardware wallet makers are now auditing their own code.
Coldcard is working directly with affected users on fund recovery and probing whether the flaw was exploited before disclosure.

items.title: Russia bans crypto mining in Moscow and parts of Kursk Oblast until 2032
points: Ban runs through the end of 2032, citing risk that mining (the energy-intensive computing that validates blockchain transactions) could consume 1 GW of grid capacity.
Move contrasts with Russia's broader regulatory push toward legitimizing mining elsewhere.

items.title: Taskmarket launches USDC-prize marketplace for AI agents
points: AI agents compete on open tasks and earn USDC (a dollar-pegged stablecoin) prizes judged on quality; current challenges include building Civilization I and GTA1 clones.
Entry is free with no cost to losing, removing financial barriers to participation.

Daydreams published a performance guide: persistent worker roles with memory, strict brief-to-checklist conversion, real media generation over prose, three directed revision passes, and banking reusable skills.

items.title: Single Seoul equity print triggers $57–80M in Hyperliquid liquidations
points: An SK Hynix share printed 29.96% below the prior close in Seoul pre-market, feeding TradeXYZ's Hyperliquid perpetual (a derivative tracking an asset's price with no expiry) and liquidating ~960 long accounts on August 28.
TradeXYZ holds 90%+ of HIP-3 (Hyperliquid's equity perps) open interest and 98% of builder-market volume; HIP-3 went from 2% to 50% of total perp volume since January, hitting $98B in 30-day volume.
Cause traced to corrupted TradFi limit-order-book data read by all providers, not a crypto oracle failure — TradeXYZ's onchain order book held steadier than the external feed.

items.title: Active crypto VC firms fall to 150, lowest since 2020
points: July count of 150 active investors is down 87% from the May 2022 peak of 1,177 and the lowest since November 2020.
Smaller funds, family offices, and 2021–22 angel syndicates are exiting while institutional players consolidate capital.
Dragonfly Capital, which closed a $650M fund in February, keeps deploying into infrastructure and real-world assets.
Dragonfly managing partner Haseeb Qureshi warned dedicated crypto VCs could lose relevance by 2030 as dominant platforms absorb users and liquidity.

issues.subject: A Coldcard Firmware Bug Just Drained Millions in Bitcoin

headlines: Coldcard hardware wallet firmware bug enabled attackers to drain millions in Bitcoin from affected users through a vulnerability in transaction signing
The vulnerability affected multiple firmware versions of Coldcard, a popular self-custody device designed to secure crypto assets offline away from internet-connected computers
Coldcard has released a patched firmware version and is investigating the scope of affected wallets while users are advised to move funds to secure wallets immediately

sections.title: Coldcard Vulnerability Details
points: Firmware bug in Coldcard's transaction signing mechanism allowed unauthorized access to private keys (the cryptographic credentials needed to authorize Bitcoin transfers)
Vulnerability impacted users running older and some current firmware versions of the device before the patch was released
Attack required physical or USB access to affected devices, though some reports suggest remote exploitation vectors may exist
Total losses confirmed exceed $50 million across identified compromised wallets

sections.title: Response and Remediation
points: Coldcard released emergency firmware update to patch the vulnerability and recommended all users update immediately
Company is working with affected users to recover funds and investigating whether attackers exploited the vulnerability before the patch was disclosed
Hardware wallet industry peers are auditing their own code for similar issues following disclosure

sections.title: Industry Impact
points: Incident raises concerns about supply chain security and the security practices of hardware wallet manufacturers trusted to protect billions in crypto assets
Highlights ongoing tension between hardware wallets being 'air-gapped' (physically isolated from networks) for security versus firmware update delivery challenges
This is not the first security incident for Coldcard—previous vulnerabilities in 2023 and 2024 also required firmware patches
